### Context

This particular change here goes ahead and adds in a brand new security check, one that is specifically and particularly for the case of GCP Compute Engine, and the whole entire job and purpose of this new check is to go and detect any and all of the VM instances that happen to have been configured with multiple network interfaces attached onto them. The real, underlying concern that sits behind the whole of all of this is the fact that VMs which happen to have multiple NICs on them are, precisely as a direct result of that, able to go and act in the capacity of bridges that end up sitting right there in between networks which are genuinely and truly supposed to be kept fully, completely, and properly isolated from one another at all times, and the real danger that comes out of that is that this potentially ends up opening the door to allowing attackers to go and move laterally, making their way from one network segment across and over into another separate one that they were never intended to be able to reach in the very first place at all.

### Description

What it is that this PR actually does is go right ahead and add in a brand new GCP check, one whose entire purpose is to verify whether or not the Compute Engine instances happen to have multiple network interfaces that are configured on them. The particular way in which the check here goes about operating and doing its job is that it goes right through and very carefully and methodically evaluates each and every single last one of the VM instances that there happen to be present, and then, once it has finished up with doing that whole part, it goes on from there to report right back to the user the following particular set of results, and it does so in each and every case that it comes across:

* **PASS**: the instance in question here happens to have only just a single, solitary network interface configured on it, and nothing more than that
* **FAIL**: the instance in question here happens to have multiple network interfaces configured on it (which is to say, a grand total of 2 or more of them all told when they are counted up together)

**Note**: it is genuinely and truly worth taking a moment to bear in mind right here that those instances which happened to have been created by GKE in the first place, or else, as another possibility, instances that are being put to use in the particular role and capacity of network virtual appliances, may in fact quite legitimately, reasonably, and genuinely turn out to have a real and entirely valid need for multiple network interfaces to be present on them.

#### Changes include:

**Compute Service (`compute_service.py`):**
- Added in a `network_interfaces` field onto the `Instance` model, and this particular thing here was done specifically, intentionally, and quite deliberately in order to be able to store all of the network interface data on it going forward from this point onward

**New Check (`compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces/`)** — this is the brand new check directory that has been added for all of this

### Steps to review

1. Go ahead and review the `network_interfaces` field that has been added onto the `Instance` model over inside of the `compute_service.py` file (that is, of course, if it happens to be applicable to do so)
2. Go ahead and review the particular way and manner in which the network interfaces on each instance end up being counted up one by one inside of the `_get_instances()` method its very own self
3. Go ahead and review the check logic its very own self, that is to say, the actual logic that lives over inside of the `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces.py` file itself
4. Go ahead and review the `metadata.json` file as well, taking the time to check it over quite carefully for its overall correctness and accuracy throughout

- Are there any brand new checks at all, of any kind, that happen to be included as a part of this particular PR right here? Yes / No
    - And if so, if that does indeed turn out to be the case, then do we happen to find ourselves in a position of needing to go and update the permissions for the provider that is in question here? Please do go and take the necessary time to review this particular one over quite carefully and thoroughly.

- [ ] Review whether or not it happens to turn out to be needed to go ahead and make a change to the [Readme.md](https://github.com/prowler-cloud/prowler/blob/master/README.md) at all in this case.

+from prowler.lib.check.models import Check, Check_Report_GCP
+from prowler.providers.gcp.services.compute.compute_client import compute_client
+
+
+class compute_instance_single_network_interface(Check):
+    """
+    Ensure that VM instances have a single network interface.
+
+    This check evaluates whether Compute Engine instances are configured with only
+    one network interface to minimize network complexity and reduce attack surface.
+    - PASS: The VM instance has a single network interface.
+    - MANUAL: The VM instance is a GKE-managed instance with multiple network interfaces
+              (manual review recommended as these may legitimately require multiple interfaces).
+    - FAIL: The VM instance has multiple network interfaces (excluding GKE instances).
+    """
+
+    def execute(self) -> list[Check_Report_GCP]:
+        findings = []
+        for instance in compute_client.instances:
+            report = Check_Report_GCP(metadata=self.metadata(), resource=instance)
+            report.status = "PASS"
+
+            interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces]
+            interface_count = len(instance.network_interfaces)
+
+            if interface_count == 1:
+                report.status_extended = f"VM Instance {instance.name} has a single network interface: {interface_names[0]}."
+            elif interface_count > 1:
+                # GKE instances may legitimately require multiple network interfaces
+                if instance.name.startswith("gke-"):
+                    report.status = "MANUAL"
+                    report.status_extended = f"VM Instance {instance.name} has {interface_count} network interfaces: {', '.join(interface_names)}. This is a GKE-managed instance which may legitimately require multiple interfaces. Manual review recommended."
+                else:
+                    report.status = "FAIL"
+                    report.status_extended = f"VM Instance {instance.name} has {interface_count} network interfaces: {', '.join(interface_names)}."
+            else:
+                report.status_extended = (
+                    f"VM Instance {instance.name} has no network interfaces."
+                )
+
+            findings.append(report)
+
+        return findings

+

+        with (

+        ):
+            from prowler.providers.gcp.services.compute.compute_instance_single_network_interface.compute_instance_single_network_interface import (
+                compute_instance_single_network_interface,
+            )
+
+            check = compute_instance_single_network_interface()
+            result = check.execute()
+
+            assert len(result) == 1
+            assert result[0].status == "MANUAL"
+            assert (
+                result[0].status_extended
+                == "VM Instance gke-cluster-default-pool-12345678-abcd has 2 network interfaces: nic0, nic1. This is a GKE-managed instance which may legitimately require multiple interfaces. Manual review recommended."
+            )
+            assert result[0].resource_id == "9999999999"
+            assert result[0].project_id == GCP_PROJECT_ID
+            assert result[0].resource_name == "gke-cluster-default-pool-12345678-abcd"
